simple.meaning: מַמְתַּק (mamtaq) is a Hebrew word meaning “something sweet (literally or figuratively).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מַמְתַּק (H4477) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Nehemiah 8:10, with occurrences in Nehemiah, Song of Solomon.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַמְתַּק (H4477) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מַמְתַּק (H4477) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: מַמְתַּק (mamtaq) / H4477 is traced through Nehemiah 8:10, Song of Songs 5:16 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.
